On the left, the bed runs head-to-foot to the right and the desk’s working edge faces left into the room/furnishing area; nearby tight spacing is an access issue, not a facing error. On the right, the bed points into open floor area and the shelf’s accessible face points into the room. No marked functional front clearly faces into a wall.

judgements.title: Bedroom arrangement
judgements.note: LEFT provides open circulation to the bed’s foot/long side, nightstand, and the desk-chair area. On RIGHT, the desk’s indicated front directly meets the bed, chair 1 faces directly into chair 2, and chair 2 is tightly bounded by the bed, chair 1, and waste bin, materially limiting approach and local repositioning.

judgements.title: Living Room arrangement
judgements.note: Both rooms have believable internal volume ratios. Left: sofa/chair ≈6.5, sofa/coffee table ≈1.4, and table 2/table 1 ≈2.3. Right: sofa/coffee table ≈4.5, shelf/side table =5.4, and coffee table/TV stand ≈1.5. The thin rug’s low box volume is plausible, and no pair is specifically implausible.

judgements.title: Living Room arrangement
judgements.note: Both show plausible relationships without a clear functional obstruction. Left groups the chairs around the dining table with usable spacing, including one tucked chair. Right forms a compact two-chair group around the central table while keeping the dining table separate; that separation is not inherently inferior, and the adjacent chairs do not visibly overlap.

judgements.title: Living Room arrangement
judgements.note: LEFT’s two marked chairs face one another, forming a sensible seating relationship. On RIGHT, chair 2 faces the table, but chair 1’s front points downward along the table’s side rather than toward the table or the other chair, creating a visible orientation problem.

judgements.title: Living Room arrangement
judgements.note: The left chair sensibly faces the table, but the left sofa’s marked front points toward the nearby side wall and narrow peripheral aisle rather than the usable room interior. On the right, the sofa faces the rug/coffee-table area, while the TV stand and storage fronts face into accessible open space.

judgements.title: Living Room arrangement
judgements.note: RIGHT forms a coherent seating group: the sofa sits at the rug’s end, the side table is beside it, and the coffee table and TV stand are spaced along the room. On LEFT, the large table is flush against most of the sofa’s indicated front, visibly compromising clearance and interaction, while the coffee table is positioned behind the sofa.

judgements.title: Living Room arrangement
judgements.note: LEFT forms a coherent seating group: the two chairs directly face each other with the coffee table between them. On RIGHT, the chairs are widely offset laterally while their fronts point north and south, so they neither face each other nor both engage the nearby table; chair 1 is especially disconnected from the central grouping.

judgements.title: Bedroom arrangement
judgements.note: Both marked beds have sensible head-to-foot orientation relative to their nearby nightstands, and the right-side storage faces into open room space rather than into the wall. No marked functional front is visibly misoriented.

judgements.title: Bedroom arrangement
judgements.note: Both marked bed arrows run from the side associated with the nightstand/lamp area toward the foot, making their orientations sensible. The left storage face also points into the room for access. No marked functional front visibly faces an inappropriate direction.
